en.name: Tortilla de patatas
en.summary: Tortilla de patatas keeps 1–2 days in the refrigerator at 4 °C (40 °F) or below — take the shorter end for the fashionable runny-centred kind, which is undercooked egg, and the longer end for a firm, fully set one. It does not freeze.
en.pantry: However traditional it is to leave a tortilla out on the counter, do not. It is one of the classic Spanish Salmonella vehicles, and the reason is in the recipe: the centre is meant to be soft. Egg dishes should reach 70 °C for two seconds; for preparations that cannot, such as fried eggs and tortillas eaten immediately, the alternative is 63 °C at the centre for twenty seconds — and a tortilla poco cuajada has met neither. Refrigerate it within two hours of cooking, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: 1–2 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, covered. A runny-centred tortilla is a same-day dish and should be eaten within a day; a firm, fully set one is more forgiving and will take the second. The underlying rule is that a held egg preparation should be kept at 8 °C or below for a maximum of twenty-four hours, and the number here is that rule read against general leftover guidance and cut short because a soft tortilla never met the heat condition that allowance assumes. If you want one that keeps, cook it through, or use pasteurised egg.
en.freezer: Freezing ruins it and there is no timeline for it. Potato turns mealy and grainy when frozen and thawed, because ice crystals break down the cell walls, and cooked egg weeps water, so a thawed tortilla is a wet, crumbling thing sitting in a pool of liquid. There is no good way round this — not slicing it thin, not wrapping it tightly. Make a smaller tortilla instead, or turn the leftovers into a sandwich the next day.
spoilage: A sulphurous or sour smell rather than a clean egg-and-olive-oil one.
A slimy or tacky surface, or liquid weeping from the cut face.
A grey or greenish cast through the egg.
Any mould at the surface or on the cut edge.
tips: Cook it through if you want it to keep; a soft centre is a same-day dish.
Cool it on a rack and refrigerate within two hours, covered.
Use pasteurised egg if you are cooking for anyone vulnerable.
Eat it cold or at room temperature straight from the fridge rather than reheating it repeatedly.

faq.q: How long does tortilla de patatas keep?
faq.a: 1–2 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. A runny-centred one should be eaten within a day; a firm one will take the second.

faq.q: Can you leave a tortilla out on the counter?
faq.a: No. It is a classic Salmonella vehicle precisely because the centre is deliberately soft. Refrigerate within two hours of cooking.

faq.q: Can you freeze tortilla de patatas?
faq.a: No. The potato goes mealy and the egg weeps water. There is no good way round it.

zh.name: 西班牙馬鈴薯烘蛋
zh.summary: 西班牙馬鈴薯烘蛋冷藏 4 °C 以下可放 1～2 天——流行的「爆漿半熟」版本請取短的那一端，因為那是沒熟的蛋；完全凝固的紮實版本才取長的那一端。它不能冷凍。
zh.pantry: 不管把烘蛋放在檯面上有多傳統，請不要。它是西班牙最典型的沙門氏菌載具之一，而原因就寫在食譜裡：中心本來就要半凝固。含蛋料理應達到 70 °C 兩秒；對於做不到的即食製備（例如荷包蛋與烘蛋），替代標準是中心 63 °C 二十秒——而一份 tortilla poco cuajada 兩者都沒達到。請在烹調後兩小時內冷藏，氣溫超過 32 °C 時縮短為一小時。
zh.fridge: 加蓋放 4 °C 以下 1～2 天。半熟中心的烘蛋是當天食品，應在一天內吃完；完全凝固的紮實版本寬容一些，可以撐到第二天。背後的規則是：存放中的含蛋製備品應維持在 8 °C 以下，最多二十四小時。這裡的數字，就是把那條規則對照剩菜的一般建議、再因為「半熟烘蛋從未達到那個加熱條件」而縮短的結果。想要放得住，就把它煎熟，或改用殺菌蛋液。
zh.freezer: 冷凍會毀掉它，也沒有任何期限可言。馬鈴薯冷凍再解凍會變得粉粉沙沙的，因為冰晶破壞了細胞壁；熟蛋則會出水，所以解凍後的烘蛋是一塊濕爛易碎的東西，泡在一灘水裡。這件事沒有變通方法——切薄不行，包緊也不行。請做小一點，或隔天把剩下的夾成三明治吃掉。
spoilage: 聞起來有硫味或酸味，而不是乾淨的蛋香與橄欖油香。
表面黏滑發黏，或切面滲出液體。
tips: 想放得住就煎熟；半熟中心的是當天食品。
放在架上散熱，兩小時內加蓋冷藏。
做給高風險族群吃時，請使用殺菌蛋液。
從冰箱拿出來冷食或回到室溫再吃，不要反覆回熱。

faq.q: 西班牙烘蛋可以放多久？
faq.a: 冷藏 4 °C 以下 1～2 天。半熟中心的請在一天內吃完，完全凝固的可以到第二天。
不行。它之所以是沙門氏菌的典型載具，正是因為中心刻意保持半熟。請在烹調後兩小時內冷藏。

faq.q: 西班牙烘蛋可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 不行。馬鈴薯會變粉、蛋會出水，沒有變通方法。
